name: Daily Top Three
title: Pick tomorrow's top three tasks before today ends.
benefit: A focused start and more meaningful progress.
subtitle: Daily Planning
rationale: Choosing tomorrow's work while today's context is still loaded means the morning starts in execution rather than triage.

evidence.summary: A century-old practitioner method (Ivy Lee) still used by top operators; plausible via decision-fatigue research but untested directly.

indications: Mornings open with list-sorting instead of work.
Task lists grow faster than they shrink.
The important task keeps losing to the easy one.
